title: Criteria for Merging Schools and Junior Colleges
what_it_is: Criteria for Merging Schools and Junior Colleges

sections.label: School merger criteria and staff
sections.summary: Questions ask the Minister for Education about merger criteria, name and premises decisions, consultation, and preparing teaching staff for mergers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: asked	the Minister for Education (Schools) in respect of the merger of schools and junior colleges (a) what are the criteria used to decide on how the respective schools or colleges will merge with their respective counterparts; (b) what are the criteria used to decide on which school or junior college should give up the use of their name or existing premises after the merger; and (c) whether all the affected schools and junior colleges have been consulted prior to the decision by the Ministry.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
sentences.text: asked	the Minister for Education (Schools) in view of the smaller enrolment of students in the longer term (a) how can our teaching staff be prepared for school mergers; and (b) how can training be provided to give them more redeployment options.

sections.label: Junior college critical mass questions
sections.summary: Questions ask the Minister for Education about minimum JC critical mass, post-merger cut-off points, and why a merger alternative was rejected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: asked	the Minister for Education (Schools) (a) what is the junior college enrolment size that is deemed to constitute minimum "critical mass"; (b) what is the expected percentage of total JC places with a cut-off point at or over 10, post-merger of the JCs; and (c) why did the Ministry reject the option of retaining the four JCs slated for the merger and reducing class size with some programmes operated on a cluster basis with JCs or Institutes, as necessary.

sections.label: MOE school merger pairs
sections.summary: Since 2015, MOE has merged or announced mergers of 18 pairs of schools, including four pairs merging in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Since 2015, MOE has merged or announced the mergers of 18 pairs of schools, including four pairs that would be merging in 2018.

sections.label: JC1 intake projected fall
sections.summary: JC1 intake is projected to fall 20%, from 16,000 students in 2010 to around 12,800 in 2019, equal to four typical JCs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: The JC1 intake is projected to fall by 20%, from 16,000 students in 2010 to around 12,800 students in 2019.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: This fall of 3,200 JC1 students is equal to the intake for four typical JCs.

sections.label: JC1 intake and capacity
sections.summary: For 2018, JC1 intake for remaining JCs will increase, with sufficient capacity so no JC-eligible student is denied a place.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: For 2018, we plan to increase the JC1 student intake for the remaining JCs and we have sufficient capacity in our JCs to ensure that no JC-eligible student would be denied a place.

sections.label: Guaranteed JC place
sections.summary: A student who qualifies for JC and chooses to go there will have a JC place.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Most importantly, a student who qualifies for JC and chooses to go there, will have a JC place.

sections.label: No retrenchment for MOE staff
sections.summary: MOE staff are assured they will not be retrenched in all school mergers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: For all school mergers, we have assured our MOE staff that they will not be retrenched.

sections.label: Support for redeployed teachers
sections.summary: Receiving schools pair redeployed teachers with buddies, adjust workloads, and MOE helps them transition smoothly.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: The receiving schools will pair each redeployed teacher with a buddy or mentor and provide a supportive environment to ensure a smooth transition.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: We also encourage schools to, where possible, adjust the workload for cross-deployed teachers in their first year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: MOE is committed as a system to help these teachers transit smoothly so that our teachers continue to make a positive difference in our students.

sections.label: Postings, culture fit, pedagogical support
sections.summary: Postings consider skills, needs, culture and socio-emotional fit, with courses and training for unfamiliar work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: It is very different in the way they do things, whether it is IP schools, non-IP schools or other schools.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: This is a combination of finding appropriate postings on the basis of skills as well as needs, and we do take into account the compatibility of the culture and socio-emotional aspects.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: We also provide pedagogical support, additional courses and training for staff who may be doing something that they are not familiar with, especially if they have been used to teaching a particular subject or level for many number of years.

sections.label: Merger pairs not pre-tested
sections.summary: The specific merger pairs could not be extensively tested before the decision was made.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: As I have explained, the announcement of the specific merger pairs was not something that we could test the waters with extensively before a decision was made.

sections.label: Staff anxiety and geographical spread
sections.summary: Staff feel anxiety changing jobs, but merged pairs were arranged for a good geographical spread of JC places.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: There is anxiety when staff have to change jobs, to do something that they have not been doing, to move from one place of work to another.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: But we did try as far as possible to ensure that the merged pairs result in a good geographical spread of JC places across the nation.

sections.label: Preserving school ethos and heritage
sections.summary: Mergers aim to preserve schools' ethos and values through niche programmes, CCAs, renaming, history and heritage.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: It is not about whether it is a low-enrolment school or a high-enrolment school.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: So, we are trying as hard as possible to preserve the ethos and values of these schools when we merge them, through the preservation of their niche programmes, CCAs, engagements with the renaming, the history and the heritage.

sections.label: Stakeholder engagement in merging schools
sections.summary: All stakeholders in merging schools have been consulted and remain engaged, including staff, students and alumni, with engagement ongoing.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: All the stakeholders in all the merging schools have been consulted and continue to be engaged with thoroughly − staff, students, alumni − and the engagement is ongoing as we have to think of names and various other aspects.

sections.label: JC pathway graduate education proportion
sections.summary: The expectation is that the proportion of a cohort applying for the JC pathway and then seeking graduate education is likely to stay the same.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: To the first question, our anticipation is that the proportion of a given cohort that will apply for the JC pathway and then seek a graduate education is likely to be the same.

sections.label: Exploring options for falling enrolment
sections.summary: A wide range of possibilities for dealing with falling enrolment was explored, and in 2010 three schools were used to increase diversity and house the IP Programme.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: We explored a wide range of possibilities to deal with this problem.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: I cannot speak specifically of the processes in 2010 but, certainly, across time, we have explored a wide variety of possibilities of how we might deal with falling enrolment, whether we need to change the models of some of the JCs, go for smaller JCs, go for larger JCs, including some of the suggestions that the Member has made.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: It was the larger reason that, system wide, we wanted to preserve a number of outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: We wanted to have, in 2010, the three schools that we talked about to increase diversity in our landscape and provide a receptacle for the IP Programme for the secondary schools that I spoke about in my earlier response.

sections.label: Forward planning for JC capacity
sections.summary: The question asks what lessons were drawn on forward planning for new JCs and capacity, noting fewer JC choices and longer travel for some students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: So, have there been any lessons drawn about how we can improve the forward planning in terms of establishing new JCs, establishing more capacity for JC places?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It would appear that the number of JC choices available to such students would now be diminished and that would mean that there would be longer travel time for such students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: For example, 14 to 16 pointers in the east would have fewer JC options, and students in the west with 10 to 12 points would have fewer options as well.

sections.label: Assistance for non-teaching staff and vendors
sections.summary: The question asks what measures are being taken to assist administrative non-teaching staff and vendors, such as canteen and shop operators and lab technicians, in the transition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Lastly, on the fate of administrative non-teaching staff and vendors in the JCs, I would like to ask about vendors, such as canteen operators, shop operators, lab technicians and so on, what measures are being taken to assist them in the transition.

sections.label: Increase in JC places 2005-2012
sections.summary: Between 2005 and 2012 JC places were significantly increased, with packed classrooms at maximised capacity during peak student cohort sizes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Between 2005 and 2012, we significantly rammed up JC places.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: We had packed classrooms because we had maximised the capacity, because that was when we had the peak student cohort sizes going through.

sections.label: Uncertainty in births and choices
sections.summary: The passage states there is uncertainty about future births and about students' choices regarding a new or merged JC.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: We have a window, we know about the births that already happened, we do not know about births that have not happened yet.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: There is some uncertainty in this, just as there is uncertainty about the choices that students would make over the popularity of a new JC or a merged JC.
